text.en: In Sakhalin Ainu, /u/ is rounded rather than unrounded like Japanese, and is close to /o/ ⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-u-is-rounded-rather-than⟧. In open monosyllabic words in Sakhalin Ainu, the vowels are all long—as in *cii*, *nii*, *ee*, *ree*, *aa*, *maa*, *too*, *poo*, *kuu*, *nuu*, and *ruu*—and their pitch accent is all high ⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-vowel-of-an-open⟧⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-vowels-in-open-monosyllabic-words⟧. Accented vowels in open syllables in Sakhalin Ainu are likewise long, as shown by *niirus*, *heese*, *yeene*, *haacin*, *aane*, *pookero*, *tookes*, *tuitas*, and *huure* ⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-accented-vowels-in-open-syllables⟧. In contrast, vowels of closed syllables ending in the sonorants or fricatives */s, m, n, w, y, r/* are always short in Sakhalin Ainu ⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-vowels-of-closed-syllables⟧. The root vowel in a single-syllable word in Karafuto dialects may be long, as in *puu* and *kii*, but it becomes short when a suffix is attached, as in *ki-hci* ⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--the-root-vowel-in-a-single-syllable-word⟧. Many vowels bearing a high accent in many Hokkaido dialects are lengthened in Karafuto dialects, as in Hokkaido *káni* and *sések* corresponding to Karafuto *kaani* and *seeseh* ⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--many-vowels-that-bear-a-high-accent-in⟧. Long vowels in Sakhalin Ainu and high pitch accent in Hokkaido Ainu do not necessarily stand in a one-to-one relationship, and there are several cases where a syllable with low pitch in Hokkaido corresponds to a long vowel in Sakhalin ⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--there-are-several-cases-where-a-syllable-with⟧⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--long-vowels-in-sakhalin-ainu-and-high-pitch⟧. Itabashi proposes that the relationship between Hokkaido and Sakhalin Ainu cannot be properly understood unless pitch accent as well as vowel length is recognized as phonemically distinctive ⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--the-relationship-between-hokkaido-and-sakhalin-ainu-cannot⟧. Regarding Hokkaido Ainu, Tamura attested from fieldwork with Tasuke Yamamoto that his idiolect in Kushiro did not have a phonemic distinction between long and short vowels ⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--suzuko-tamura-attested-that-from-her-direct-fieldwork⟧.
text.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、/u/は日本語のように非円唇ではなく円唇であり、/o/に近い⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-u-is-rounded-rather-than⟧。樺太アイヌ語では開音節の単音節語の母音はすべて長く、ピッチアクセントもすべて高くなり、*cii*、*nii*、*ee*、*ree*、*aa*、*maa*、*too*、*poo*、*kuu*、*nuu*、*ruu*がこれに該当する⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-vowel-of-an-open⟧⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-vowels-in-open-monosyllabic-words⟧。樺太アイヌ語において開音節でアクセントのある母音もまた長く、*niirus*、*heese*、*yeene*、*haacin*、*aane*、*pookero*、*tookes*、*tuitas*、*huure*の例がある⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-accented-vowels-in-open-syllables⟧。一方で、音節末尾音が/s, m, n, w, y, r/である閉音節の母音は樺太方言において常に短い⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-vowels-of-closed-syllables⟧。樺太方言において単音節語の語根母音は*puu*や*kii*のように長母音になりうるが、接尾辞が付くと*ki-hci*のように短母音になる⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--the-root-vowel-in-a-single-syllable-word⟧。北海道の多くの方言で高アクセントをもつ母音の多くは樺太方言において長母音化しており、北海道方言の*káni*や*sések*に対して樺太方言の*kaani*や*seeseh*が対応する⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--many-vowels-that-bear-a-high-accent-in⟧。樺太アイヌ語の長母音と北海道アイヌ語の高いアクセントは必ずしも1対1の関係にはなく、北海道方言でピッチが低い音節が樺太方言で長母音に対応する例もいくつか見られる⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--there-are-several-cases-where-a-syllable-with⟧⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--long-vowels-in-sakhalin-ainu-and-high-pitch⟧。板橋は、母音の長短だけでなくピッチアクセントも音韻的弁別上の特徴と見なさなければ、北海道と樺太の関係は正しく認識できないと提起している⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--the-relationship-between-hokkaido-and-sakhalin-ainu-cannot⟧。北海道アイヌ語に関しては、田村すず子が生前の山本多助に対する直接調査に基づき、山本の個人語（釧路方言）には母音の長短の区別が存在しなかったと証言している⟦claim:phon/vowel-inventory--suzuko-tamura-attested-that-from-her-direct-fieldwork⟧。
